solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Nobbled horse – a thing attempting to unseat leader? (4,7)

annotation.definitionNote: a verb phrase standing in for the crime it describes, a noun

indicatorNotes.Nobbled: a nobbled horse has been tampered with, so its letters are interfered with too

annotation.surface: A racecourse scandal: someone has got at a horse to throw its jockey.
annotation.walkthrough: The racing picture makes the leader a jockey on a horse; the definition reads it as a monarch, and plotting to overthrow one is high treason.
annotation.definitionFit: High treason is the crime of trying to overthrow or kill the sovereign.

entries.clue: Joint payment arrangement includes one (3)

indicatorNotes.includes: the arrangement holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: HP = hire purchase, paying in instalments

annotation.surface: A shared payment plan that takes in one more party.
annotation.walkthrough: HP (hire purchase) is the British name for buying on instalments; 'Joint' looks like an adjective with 'payment', but it is the body part.
annotation.definitionFit: The hip is the joint between thigh and pelvis.

entries.clue: German linguist dour in broadcast (5)

indicatorNotes.in broadcast: what goes out over the air is heard, not read

blocks.note: dour = stern and gloomy; the surname's double M is silent

annotation.surface: A humourless German scholar giving a talk on the wireless.
annotation.walkthrough: Jacob Grimm, of the fairy-tale brothers, was a serious philologist who gave his name to Grimm's law of sound change.
annotation.definitionFit: Jacob Grimm was a German linguist, famous for Grimm's law.

entries.clue: Small group’s small outing? (7)

blocks.note: -let is the suffix for something small, as in piglet

annotation.surface: A little group of people heading off on a modest day out.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the answer as TRIP-LET and it is literally a small outing, which is the joke the question mark flags.
annotation.definitionFit: A triplet is a set of three, such as three notes played in the time of two.

entries.clue: Optical issue certainly apparent in damaged retina (9)

indicatorNotes.apparent in: the first word shows up inside the second
indicatorNotes.damaged: the retina's letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: yes = certainly, placed after the E

annotation.surface: An eye doctor reporting a clear problem visible in a damaged retina.
annotation.walkthrough: The eye-clinic surface keeps 'retina' looking like part of the diagnosis rather than a jumble of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain description: tired, aching eyes from overuse are a complaint of sight, which is what 'optical' covers.

entries.clue: That woman starts to boss all in queen’s place (5)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take only the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of boss and all

annotation.surface: A domineering woman bossing everyone about in the queen's household.
annotation.walkthrough: The Queen of Sheba visited Solomon in the Bible, so her kingdom is the queen's place.
annotation.definitionFit: Sheba is the ancient land ruled by the Queen of Sheba.

entries.clue: Salt turned up in stock (7)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning a word up writes it from bottom to top

blocks.note: a stock phrase is a trite one

annotation.surface: A cook finding salt has shown up in the soup stock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is the reversed piece; 'stock' is the adjective, as in stock response.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: chemists call any compound formed from an acid a salt, and this one comes from nitrous acid.

entries.clue: Manner of one expected to succeed on radio (3)

indicatorNotes.on radio: radio is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: an heir expects to inherit; its H is silent

annotation.surface: A radio presenter's bearing, as the one lined up to take over.
annotation.walkthrough: HEIR begins with a silent H, so it is said exactly like AIR.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the sense of bearing, as in someone having an air of confidence about them.

entries.clue: Untrustworthy sort breaking trade rule (9)

indicatorNotes.breaking: the rule is broken apart and its letters reset

annotation.surface: A dodgy dealer flouting the regulations of commerce.
annotation.walkthrough: The business surface points to a cheat in trade; the answer is unfaithful in marriage instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: someone who cheats on a spouse has broken a vow of trust.

entries.clue: Cup match perhaps cut short to fix substitute (11)

indicatorNotes.cut short: the last letter is lopped off

annotation.surface: A football cup tie ended early so that a substitute can be arranged.
annotation.walkthrough: In English cup football a drawn tie is settled by a replay, which is why 'perhaps' is there.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, and the football surface fits: a player coming off the bench is called either.

entries.clue: Puritan concealing disgusting source of extreme advantage (9)

indicatorNotes.concealing: the puritan hides the next word inside him
indicatorNotes.source of: a word's source is where it starts, its first letter

blocks.note: a prig is a self-righteous prude

annotation.surface: A puritan hiding a nasty secret that is the source of his great advantage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extreme' looks like it qualifies 'advantage', but only its first letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a benefit enjoyed by some and not others, as in the privileges of rank.

entries.clue: Beat corporation power, securing hope initially (5)

indicatorNotes.securing: the belly holds the next letter inside
indicatorNotes.initially: at first, so only the word's opening letter is used

blocks.note: corporation = paunch, TUM, plus P for power
first letter of hope, held after the T

annotation.surface: A company's power to crush people's hopes at the outset.
annotation.walkthrough: Corporation is old slang for a pot belly, hence TUM; the business sense is the decoy.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as a verb: to hit hard with the fist.

entries.clue: Drew near to line twisting around castle (7)

indicatorNotes.twisting around: the pair of pieces is turned back to front

blocks.note: TO plus L for line, then turned round

annotation.surface: Someone approaching a winding rope that loops round a castle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' is not a link word here; it is two of the letters, joined by L for line.
annotation.definitionFit: Camelot is King Arthur's legendary castle and court.

entries.clue: Noticed iron tainted cosmetic (11)

indicatorNotes.tainted: the letters are spoiled into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone spotting that a beauty product is contaminated with iron.
annotation.walkthrough: The product-recall surface makes 'tainted' look like a description when it is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a hair treatment sold beside shampoo is one of many cosmetics.

entries.clue: Song I’m obliged to follow that is limited by technique (7)

indicatorNotes.limited by: the phrase is enclosed by the technique
indicatorNotes.to follow: this piece comes after the rest

blocks.note: ta = thanks, what you say when obliged

annotation.surface: A singer told that a particular song must come next, within the limits of technique.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I'm obliged' is a phrase of thanks, and TA is informal British for thank you.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: a short aria, the Italian diminutive, is a kind of song.

entries.clue: Black king evading opponent’s piece? (5)

indicatorNotes.evading: the king escapes from the piece, leaving it

blocks.note: a knight is a chess piece

annotation.surface: A chess move: Black's king slips away from the other side's piece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Black' looks like the chess side but is the definition: the dark of night.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun sense of 'black': the darkness after sunset, as in black of the night.

entries.clue: Information on each record linked to unknown family history (9)

annotation.surface: A researcher linking each record to an unknown ancestor.
annotation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information, as in getting the gen on something.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: tracing lines of descent is exactly the study of a family's history.

entries.clue: Software permitted water plant to be trimmed in part of orchard (5,4)

indicatorNotes.to be trimmed: the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: an app is a piece of software

annotation.surface: Software that allows a waterside plant to be pruned in an orchard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Software' and 'permitted' read as a computing surface, but each is simply a short synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: An orchard is made up of fruit trees, such as apple trees.

entries.clue: Fix earlier account, deleting chapter in distress (9)

indicatorNotes.deleting: the chapter's letter is taken out
indicatorNotes.in: what remains goes inside the distress

blocks.note: pain = distress, wrapped round the rest

annotation.surface: Someone correcting an earlier account while a chapter is cut in distress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fix earlier account' reads as one phrase; the definition stops after 'earlier'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym built from its parts: PRE- means earlier and ORDAIN means to decree or fix.

entries.clue: Lack of knowledge? An opening for college in blighted region (9)

indicatorNotes.opening for: the opening of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.in: AN and the C are placed within the rearranged region
indicatorNotes.blighted: the region's letters are ruined into a new order

blocks.note: REGION rearranged, wrapped round the next pieces

annotation.surface: A college opening up in a deprived area where knowledge is lacking.
annotation.walkthrough: The rearranged REGION splits as IGNOR…E, with AN and C slotted in before the E.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym; the question mark nods to the surface, where a new college is what a deprived area needs.

entries.clue: Practical approach is entrenched in field (7)

indicatorNotes.is entrenched in: dug into the field, so placed inside it

blocks.note: a realm is a field or domain

annotation.surface: A sensible method that has become firmly rooted in its field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' does double duty in the surface, as the verb and as the letters that go in.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: dealing with things as they are rather than as one wishes is the practical attitude.

entries.clue: Golf beset by dreadful sound of woe (5)

blocks.note: G = golf in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A golfer's miserable round, greeted with groans.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a bad day on the course; golf is simply the letter G.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a lament sung at a funeral is a sorrowful sound.

entries.clue: Pair of images: basin, then tiny gutted church (7)

indicatorNotes.gutted: the insides are removed, leaving the outside letters

blocks.note: a dip is a hollow or basin in the ground

annotation.surface: An altarpiece of two panels found in a basin inside a tiny, stripped church.
annotation.walkthrough: A diptych is a two-panel painting, often hinged, common as a church altarpiece.
annotation.definitionFit: A diptych is an artwork made of two matching panels.

entries.clue: Statement from ally indicating religious position (7)

blocks.note: what a friend declares to you, contraction and all, run together

annotation.surface: Someone declaring friendship, which reveals where they stand on religion.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a whole sentence a friend might say, read without its apostrophe and spaces; an imam leads prayers in a mosque.
annotation.definitionFit: An imamate is the office of an imam, a religious post.

entries.clue: With wicket falling, blocks snicks (5)

indicatorNotes.falling: the wicket drops out of the word

blocks.note: W = wicket in cricket scoring, removed

annotation.surface: A cricket commentary: a batsman snicks the ball and a wicket falls.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket a snick or edge is a thin touch off the side of the bat; 'blocks' also sounds like a defensive shot, but it is the wedges.
annotation.definitionFit: To edge the ball is to snick it off the bat.

entries.clue: Endless drama in accommodation cost? Move elsewhere (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the drama goes inside the cost

blocks.note: rent is the cost of housing, wrapped round the rest

annotation.surface: A never-ending row over rent, settled by moving house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Move elsewhere' sounds like moving house, but the answer is gardening: moving a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: To replant is to move a plant to a new spot.

entries.clue: From the outset, not entirely too proud for love (2,3)

indicatorNotes.not entirely: the word is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: ABOVE, as in above doing something, missing its E

annotation.surface: Someone who, from the very start, was a little too haughty to fall in love.
annotation.walkthrough: Ab ovo is Latin for 'from the egg', meaning from the very beginning.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin phrase, literally 'from the egg', used in English for starting at the very beginning.

entries.clue: Biblical character reflected one lament (5)

indicatorNotes.reflected: a mirror image, so written backwards

blocks.note: moan = lament; I MOAN is then reversed

annotation.surface: A figure from scripture thinking back on a grief.
annotation.walkthrough: Naomi fits: in the Book of Ruth she laments her losses and asks to be called Mara, bitter.
annotation.definitionFit: Naomi is Ruth's mother-in-law in the Old Testament.

entries.clue: Unexpected money club’s carrying round? It’s on the table (5,4)

indicatorNotes.carrying: the club holds the round inside it

annotation.surface: A windfall from a club paying for a round of drinks, with the cash laid on the table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the table' suggests money or an offer, but it is literal: a jug for gravy at dinner.
annotation.definitionFit: Cryptic-style description: a boat-shaped jug for sauce is laid out with the dinner, so it is on the table.

entries.clue: Fix cup match (3)

blocks.note: fix = fasten, as with a knot
British name for a knockout cup fixture

annotation.surface: Rigging a cup game.
annotation.walkthrough: Fixing a match suggests cheating, but each word is a plain definition; in British football a cup match is a tie.
annotation.definitionFit: Tie means both fasten and a knockout cup game.

entries.clue: Beam of light ready to be periodically blocked (3)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular intervals, so every other letter

blocks.note: keep the first, third and fifth letters
the E and D are blocked out

annotation.surface: A light beam set up and then intermittently obstructed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blocked' is part of the instruction: the letters in between are shut out.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as in a ray of sunshine through a window.

entries.clue: I am mostly the person that’s ill-disposed? (11)

annotation.definition: I am mostly the person that’s ill-disposed?

indicatorNotes.mostly: the next word loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A grumpy confession: I'm pretty much the one who dislikes everybody.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the instruction and the definition: someone ill-disposed to people is a misanthrope.
annotation.definitionFit: A misanthrope dislikes other people, so is ill-disposed.
